raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, MiniMax-M3 on MI350X gives a long prompt different tokens depending on how many requests share its decode batch: a 4k-token prompt matches its batch-size-1 output in batches of 2-8 requests and differs from 16 requests up, whatever the other requests are. The sparse-attention decode kernels choose their split-K chunk counts from the batch size (`flash_decode_with_topk_idx`: `NUM_KV_CHUNKS` from `4096 // (batch_size * num_kv_heads)`; `flash_decode_with_gqa_share_sparse`: `NUM_TOPK_CHUNKS` from `256 // (batch_size * num_kv_heads)`), and on gfx950 the decode score kernel uses a 512-token tile for batches of up to 4 requests and 128 above. Each choice changes the order in which a request's partial results are combined, so its output depends on its batch mates. This PR sizes them for a fixed batch size (16) in deterministic mode. Normal mode is unchanged.

## Modifications

- `minimax_sparse/common/utils.py`: `grid_batch_size(batch_size)` returns 16 when deterministic inference is on (read once from the runtime config) and `batch_size` otherwise.
- `decode/flash_with_topk_idx.py`: the KV chunk count and the gfx950 score-tile choice use `grid_batch_size(batch_size)`.
- `decode/topk_sparse.py`: the top-k chunk count uses `grid_batch_size(batch_size)`.
- New test `test/registered/amd/test_minimax_sparse_decode_batch_invariant.py` (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`): in deterministic mode, a request decoded alone and among 1-63 other requests (random lengths 2k-8k tokens, random position) gives bitwise identical results with MiniMax-M3's head layouts: the indexer's top-k blocks (score-only, as MiniMax-M3's sparse layers run it) and the sparse attention output; plus the grid-size helper.
- Unchanged: normal mode, other models.

16 is the count of a mid-size batch: at batch size 1 the kernels would launch many more CTAs than needed for large batches (the batch-size-1 counts cost 5.8% decode throughput at 1k in / 1k out, against 3.4% for 16).

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, ROCm 7.2.4, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`, MiniMax-M3 (MXFP4), TP2, deterministic mode, together with a deterministic MXFP4 MoE path (not part of this PR; the model's MoE is otherwise not deterministic on this image) and the fp32 router gate (`SGLANG_OPT_USE_BF16_ROUTER_GEMM=0`).

`python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic` (`single`, `prefix`, `prefix --return-logprob`, `radix_cache`, 50 trials) plus a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response):

| | before | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `single` | 1 output | 1 output |
| `prefix` (4 prompts, outputs per prompt) | 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 |
| `prefix --return-logprob` | logprobs differ | identical |
| bitwise batch-size check | 1,275 / 1,275 | 1,275 / 1,275 |
| 4k-token prompt in batches of 2-50 (25 cases) | differs from 16 requests up | 25 / 25 identical |

With this branch's files the checks above pass on 2 / 2 fresh servers (the table's "this PR" column was measured with the same logic behind an experiment-only switch, on 3 / 3 more fresh servers). GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.2, temperature 0, 1,319 questions): 95.60%. The new test passes on MI350X (`7 passed`); with deterministic mode off it fails (4 of 7: the sparse attention output at every layout and the grid-size check; the top-k selection matches either way, since the max block scores do not depend on the split).

Scope: these results are at TP2. At TP4 MiniMax-M3 shows a separate difference through the prefix cache (a cached prefix vs a fresh prefill), which this PR does not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Deterministic mode, MiniMax-M3 TP2, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, output throughput:

| workload | before | this PR | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k in / 1k out, 256 prompts | 2,383 tok/s | 2,302 tok/s | -3.4% |
| 8k in / 1k out, 128 prompts | 588.2 tok/s | 582.2 tok/s | -1.0% |

Normal mode is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

     return 1.0 if scale is None else scale
 
 
+# The decode kernels size their split-K grids (and the gfx950 score tile) from the
+# batch size, so a request's reduction order depends on how many requests share its
+# batch. --enable-deterministic-inference sizes them for this batch size instead,
+# whatever the real one.
+DETERMINISTIC_GRID_BATCH_SIZE = 16
+

+
+        try:
+            exec_cfg = get_exec()
+        except ValueError:

+        )
+    return _deterministic_inference
+
+
+def grid_batch_size(batch_size: int) -> int:
+    """The batch size the decode kernels size their grids and tiles for."""
+    if _is_deterministic_inference():
+        return DETERMINISTIC_GRID_BATCH_SIZE
+    return batch_size
+

@@ -0,0 +1,159 @@
+"""MiniMax sparse-attention decode sizes its split-K grids (and, on gfx950, the score
+tile) from the batch size. With --enable-deterministic-inference they are sized for a
+fixed batch size instead, so a request's output must not depend on its batch: decode
+one request alone and among other requests, and compare its rows bit for bit.
+"""
+
+import random
+import sys
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.common import utils as sparse_utils
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.decode.flash_with_topk_idx import (
+    flash_decode_with_topk_idx,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.minimax_sparse.decode.topk_sparse import (
+    flash_decode_with_gqa_share_sparse,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=60, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+
+HEAD_DIM = 128
+BLOCK_SIZE = 128
+TOPK = 16
+NUM_REQS = 64
+MAX_KV_LEN = 8192
+BATCH_SIZES = [2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 16, 17, 32, 64]
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _deterministic_mode():
+    with patch.object(sparse_utils, "_is_deterministic_inference", return_value=True):
+        yield
+
+
+def _pool(num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, seed):
+    """K/V and a req_to_token row for NUM_REQS requests; batches pick rows by slot id."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    kv_shape = (NUM_REQS * MAX_KV_LEN, num_kv_heads, HEAD_DIM)
+    k, v = (
+        torch.randn(kv_shape, generator=g, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        for _ in range(2)
+    )
+    q = torch.randn(
+        NUM_REQS,
+        num_q_heads,
+        HEAD_DIM,
+        generator=g,
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    )
+    req_to_token = torch.arange(
+        NUM_REQS * MAX_KV_LEN, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    ).view(NUM_REQS, MAX_KV_LEN)
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    seq_lens = [rng.randint(TOPK * BLOCK_SIZE, MAX_KV_LEN) for _ in range(NUM_REQS)]
+    return (
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        req_to_token,
+        torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+    )
+
+
+def _batches(seed):
+    """(target position, slot ids) for batches of every size, the target request 0 at
+    a random position among random batchmates."""
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    for bs in BATCH_SIZES:
+        mates = rng.sample(range(1, NUM_REQS), bs - 1)
+        pos = rng.randrange(bs)
+        yield pos, mates[:pos] + [0] + mates[pos:]
+
+
+# MiniMax-M3's sparse-layer indexer at TP1 / TP2 / TP8: index heads per KV head, scores
+# only (its sparse layers disable the index-value output).
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_q_heads,num_kv_heads", [(4, 4), (2, 2), (8, 1)])
+def test_flash_decode_with_topk_idx_batch_invariant(num_q_heads, num_kv_heads):
+    q, k, v, req_to_token, seq_lens = _pool(num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, seed=0)
+
+    def run(slots):
+        ids = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        lens = seq_lens[ids]
+        _, topk_idx, _ = flash_decode_with_topk_idx(
+            q[ids],
+            None,
+            k,
+            v,
+            req_to_token,
+            lens,
+            int(lens.max().item()),
+            ids,
+            BLOCK_SIZE,
+            TOPK,
+            0,
+            1,
+            disable_index_value=True,
+        )
+        return topk_idx
+
+    alone = run([0])
+    for pos, slots in _batches(seed=1):
+        assert torch.equal(run(slots)[:, pos], alone[:, 0]), f"batch of {len(slots)}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_q_heads,num_kv_heads", [(64, 4), (32, 2), (16, 1)])
+def test_flash_decode_with_gqa_share_sparse_batch_invariant(num_q_heads, num_kv_heads):
+    q, k, v, req_to_token, seq_lens = _pool(num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, seed=2)
+    rng = random.Random(3)
+    # TOPK distinct blocks per request and kv head, inside the request's context
+    blocks = torch.tensor(
+        [
+            [
+                sorted(rng.sample(range(-(-int(n) // BLOCK_SIZE)), TOPK))
+                for n in seq_lens.tolist()
+            ]
+            for _ in range(num_kv_heads)
+        ],
+        dtype=torch.int32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+
+    def run(slots):
+        ids = torch.tensor(slots, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        return flash_decode_with_gqa_share_sparse(
+            q[ids],
+            None,
+            k,
+            v,
+            req_to_token,
+            seq_lens[ids],
+            ids,
+            BLOCK_SIZE,
+            blocks[:, ids].contiguous(),
+        )
+
+    alone = run([0])
+    for pos, slots in _batches(seed=4):
+        assert torch.equal(run(slots)[pos], alone[0]), f"batch of {len(slots)}"
+
+
+def test_grid_batch_size():
+    assert sparse_utils.grid_batch_size(1) == sparse_utils.DETERMINISTIC_GRID_BATCH_SIZE
+    assert (
+        sparse_utils.grid_batch_size(64) == sparse_utils.DETERMINISTIC_GRID_BATCH_SIZE
+    )
+    with patch.object(sparse_utils, "_is_deterministic_inference", return_value=False):
+        assert sparse_utils.grid_batch_size(1) == 1
+        assert sparse_utils.grid_batch_size(64) == 64
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))
